Lay a frame of records out as a listing

Source: R/table_plan.R
plan_listing.Rd

plan_listing() makes the plan a listing: a data frame of subject records (SDTM or ADaM, nothing summarised) printed through listing_spec(), with columns that can stack several variables in one cell and wrap long text. A record wrapped over several rows is not cut by a page break: it moves whole to the next page, unless it alone is longer than a page; then it is cut at the page's end and the rest goes on at the top of the next page, with no continuation row before it (a record has no heading). Its arguments are listing_spec()'s own, unchanged; the blank rows are plan_blanks()'s, as for a table.

Usage

plan_listing(
  .plan,
  ...,
  type = NULL,
  sep = NULL,
  spacer = NULL,
  spacer_rel_width = NULL,
  layout = NULL,
  wrap = NULL,
  align = NULL,
  record = NULL
)

Arguments

.plan

A table_plan() of a data frame of records.

...

The printed columns, in order: listing_col()s, or bare column names.

type

The listing template, listing_spec()'s type; the one that ships is "multiline" (the default): a "/" separator, gutter columns, a blank row after each record and one at the top of each page, text wrapped at the separator.

sep, align, layout

The defaults for the columns that set none of their own: the separator between the variables of one cell, the alignment, and "stack" (a line a part) or "flow" (filled to the column's width). NULL takes the template's.

spacer, spacer_rel_width

Whether a narrow gutter column goes between the printed columns, and its relative width. NULL takes the template's.

wrap

The rule that breaks a cell into lines, a function as listing_spec() describes; NULL the type's own (listing_wrap()).

record

The hidden record column that keeps a record on one page: TRUE (the default, NULL) under its standard name, FALSE none, or a string naming it.

Value

The plan, with one more layer.

Details

A listing cannot be combined with plan_append(): its columns are the records' own, while appended parts are a label and value columns, so plan_append() stops on a plan that carries plan_listing(), as the first plan or as a part. To show a listing with a summary, make them separate contents of the document: rtf_tables() for the listing, then rtf_tables() for the summary with page_break = FALSE (see the article "Several contents on one page").

See also

plan_verbs for every verb; listing_spec() and listing_col() for the listing in full.

Other plan verbs: plan_after(), plan_append(), plan_blanks(), plan_cell_style(), plan_cells(), plan_col_header(), plan_columns(), plan_compare(), plan_digits(), plan_empty(), plan_filter(), plan_footnotes(), plan_hide(), plan_labels(), plan_levels(), plan_nest(), plan_paginate_cols(), plan_paginate_group(), plan_paginate_rows(), plan_row_group(), plan_sort(), plan_stat_groups(), plan_stub(), plan_style(), plan_titles(), plan_total()

Examples

# Invented adverse-event records
recs <- data.frame(
  USUBJID = c("01-001", "01-001", "01-002"),
  AETERM  = c("Headache", "Nausea", "Fatigue"),
  AESEV   = c("MILD", "MODERATE", "MILD"),
  ASTDY   = c(3, 10, 5))

# Minimal: two columns; the multiline type puts a blank row after each
# record
pages <- table_plan(recs) |>
  plan_listing(listing_col("USUBJID", label = "Subject"),
               listing_col("AETERM", label = "Adverse event")) |>
  plan_apply()
pages[[1]]
#> ─────────────────────────
#> Subject     Adverse event
#> ─────────────────────────
#> 01-001      Headache     
#>                          
#> 01-001      Nausea       
#>                          
#> 01-002      Fatigue      
#>                          
#> 
#> <rtftable> 6 rows x 3 columns
#>   Columns:    Subject |  | Adverse event
#>   Row title:  col 1
#>   Borders:    set
#>   Widths:     relative 7:1:13
#> 

# The event and its severity stacked in one cell (a line each, within
# ten characters), the study day beside it; no gutter columns and no
# blank rows, for a compact listing
pages <- table_plan(recs) |>
  plan_listing(listing_col("USUBJID", label = "Subject"),
               listing_col(c("AETERM", "AESEV"), width = 10,
                           label = "Adverse event/\nSeverity"),
               listing_col("ASTDY", label = "Study day"),
               spacer = FALSE) |>
  plan_blanks(where = "none", first = FALSE) |>
  plan_apply()
pages[[1]]
#> ──────────────────────────────────
#>          Adverse event/           
#> Subject  Severity        Study day
#> ──────────────────────────────────
#> 01-001   Headache/       3        
#>          MILD                     
#> 01-001   Nausea/         10       
#>          MODERATE                 
#> 01-002   Fatigue/        5        
#>          MILD                     
#> 
#> <rtftable> 6 rows x 3 columns
#>   Columns:    Subject | Adverse event/ Severity | Study day
#>   Row title:  col 1
#>   Borders:    set
#>   Widths:     relative 7:10:9
#>
